notes.model: v3 is a dynamic factor model TRAINED ON FIRST-PRINT GDP: the quarterly target is the number the ABS published first for each quarter, not the figure it has since revised to. So its natural target is `first_print`, and that is what both v3 columns are scored against. Measured by docs/measurements/2026-09-09-plan-c-first-print-target.csv, docs/measurements/2026-09-10-plan-c-2026q2-extension-first_print.csv; the 2026-08-30 file, which measured the previous revised-target model, is not read.
notes.correction: `v3` is the PUBLISHED nowcast: the model's median less the mean of that model's own misses against the first print over the last 8 printed quarters (`nyfed/au/bias_correction.py`, seeded from this same backtest). RECURSIVE: each vintage is corrected by the misses the ABS had already printed by that vintage's date, so no row is corrected by knowledge of its own error, and the vintages before four quarters had printed carry no correction at all. `v3_model` is the same median before it.
notes.pseudo_real_time: Both models see REVISED panel data. `actual` is the latest vintage; `first_print` is what the ABS printed first, which is the number a reader saw on the day. The ABS revises quarterly growth up by about 0.1pp on average, so v2's error against `first_print` is the larger and the honest one. Panel revisions are not replayed (employment first prints run ~0.07pp/qtr stronger than the revised series, which adds to the live bias by a few hundredths). See docs/2026-09-09-unrevised-data-feasibility.md.
notes.live_quarters: The per-quarter track record in `data/performance_v3.json` replaces a backtested quarter with what was actually published where a live record exists. 2026 Q2 is the one such quarter, and it was called by the PREVIOUS model -- fitted on the revised vintage, corrected by a forty-year mean revision -- so its row there is reproduced from the history log as published (0.54, raw 0.64) and flagged `model: "revised_target"`. This file's per-vintage table is the backtest alone and does not contain it.
notes.window_start: Starts January 2023. The COVID factor runs to December 2021, so a 2022 vintage sits on its edge and v3 runs a quarter behind through it: the revised-target backtest that measured 2022 put its mean error there at 2.12pp against 0.45pp in 2024, which is why no 2022 vintage was re-run for this one.
notes.v2_config: v2 at cache/ci_recalib/qa_a10_acc.csv, its shipping backtest. Its predictor selection is fixed to the full sample, a look-ahead that flatters v2 and has no counterpart in v3.
